title: Shopping list generation (per-bucket or due-in-N-days) + plain-text export
goal: Build F12's list generator: pick a source (one cadence bucket, or everything due within N days) and materialize it into the existing, unused-since-E-0 shopping_lists/shopping_list_items tables, snapshotting each item's suggested quantity at generation time. A dedicated /shopping-list screen shows the current active list and exports it as plain text for copy/share. This directly reuses E-8's getPlanItems()/getDueSoonItems() (lib/plan/data.ts) rather than re-deriving cadence/due-date logic -- the same layering S-21/S-22 already established on top of E-7's getInventoryItems().
in_scope: lib/shopping-list/generate.ts (server-only): generateShoppingList(source: {type:'bucket', bucket: CadenceBucket} | {type:'due_in_days', days: number}) -> {id: string}. Builds candidate items from getPlanItems() (bucket source: items.cadenceBucket === bucket) or getDueSoonItems(days) (due-in-days source, reusing S-22's existing daysThreshold parameter exactly, not a re-implementation) -- BOTH sources additionally filtered to planState === 'pending' (matches getDueSoonItems' own convention; an item the user has snoozed/skipped/excluded on the Plan screen must not silently reappear on a generated shopping list -- that would undermine the whole point of those controls). Archives any existing shopping_lists row with status='active' for the household (sets status='archived') before inserting the new one, so there is at most one active list at a time -- generating replaces, never appends (no unique constraint exists on (shopping_list_id, catalog_item_id), so appending to an existing list risks duplicate rows). Inserts one shopping_lists row (status='active', name derived from the source: the bucket's display label via formatCadenceBucket, or 'Due in N days') and one shopping_list_items row per candidate item (catalog_item_id, qty_base = item.suggestedQtyBase, checked=false). Empty candidate list still creates a list with zero items (not an error) -- an empty bucket is a valid, informative outcome ('nothing due in this bucket yet'), not a failure.

lib/shopping-list/data.ts (server-only): getActiveShoppingList() -> ShoppingList | null. Reads the household's single status='active' shopping_lists row (if any) joined with its shopping_list_items and each item's catalog_items fields needed for display/export (canonical_name, brand, base_unit, default_pack_size) -- one extra query beyond a bare list, matching this repo's existing willingness to pay a small extra round trip for a live, non-drifting join (getPlanItems() does the same over getInventoryItems()). Items sorted by canonical_name for a stable, scannable list.

lib/shopping-list/format.ts (pure, no DB): formatShoppingListAsText(list: ShoppingList) -> string. Plain-text export: list name as a header line, then one line per item as '[ ] Name (brand) -- qty' or '[x] Name (brand) -- qty' for checked items, using lib/inventory/format.ts's existing formatBaseQty (no new quantity-formatting logic). This is the exact string both the clipboard-copy button and any future share/download affordance consume -- one source of truth for the exported representation.

app/shopping-list/page.tsx: server component. A 'Generate' card offering one link/button per CADENCE_BUCKET_ORDER bucket (reusing S-21's constant) plus a small due-in-N-days form (default 3, matching S-22's DEFAULT_DUE_SOON_DAYS convention) -- each posts to a server action that calls generateShoppingList and redirects back to /shopping-list. Below that, if an active list exists: its name, item count, a 'Copy as text' button (client component, lib below), and the item rows (checkbox to cross off via a plain update -- no purchase log -- plus S-24's price-logging control, added by that story). Cold-start / no active list: a plain empty state, no broken render (matches every prior screen's convention).

app/shopping-list/actions.ts ('use server'): generateShoppingListAction(source) wraps generateShoppingList, revalidatePath('/shopping-list'), redirect('/shopping-list'). setCheckedAction(shoppingListItemId, checked: boolean) does a plain shopping_list_items update of the checked column only (no ledger write -- S-24 adds the price-logging action separately) and revalidatePath('/shopping-list').

app/shopping-list/copy-list-button.tsx: 'use client'. Receives the pre-formatted plain-text string as a prop (formatShoppingListAsText already ran server-side) and calls navigator.clipboard.writeText on click, with a 2-second 'Copied' label swap for feedback -- no toast library exists in this repo yet, this matches the plain-controls convention every other screen (Plan, Inventory) already uses.
out_of_scope: Purchase-log-on-checkoff / price prompt -- S-24, this epic's second story, layers directly on top of shopping_list_items rows this story creates.

A history/archive browser for past (non-active) shopping lists -- archived lists exist in the table (for future use / debugging) but this story exposes no UI to browse them. Only the single current active list is shown.
Editing quantities or adding/removing individual items from a generated list after the fact -- the list is exactly what generation snapshotted; regenerate to pick up plan changes.

A DB migration -- shopping_lists/shopping_list_items already exist from E-0's full_schema migration with every column this story needs (name, status, qty_base, checked). Confirmed by reading the schema before writing this spec, not assumed.
acceptance: List generates from a bucket and exports as plain text (E-9 epic acceptance); List exports as plain text/clipboard for sharing (S-23's own acceptance).
invariants: generateShoppingList never appends to an existing active list -- it archives the prior active list (if any) and inserts a fresh one, so shopping_list_items never accumulates duplicate (shopping_list_id, catalog_item_id) rows across repeated generations.
Both source types (bucket, due_in_days) filter to planState==='pending' only -- an item the user snoozed, skipped, or excluded on /plan must never appear on a freshly generated shopping list.

qty_base is always populated at generation time from the live suggestedQtyBase computed by getPlanItems() -- never left null, since S-24's purchase-log path needs a real quantity to write into stock_movements without its own fallback guessing at generation-time data.
